difficulty.notes: sm-crypto (module 193c) wraps module 8060 (sm2/sm3). Password uses sm32 (n = sm2(sm3(x))); username uses sm2nokey (i) directly, so i is shared by both paths (not a clean username-only decoy). The anchor is the captured submit handler accountSubmit (the answer recorded in 1.json): it binds password->sm32 and username->sm2nokey via Object(h.b)(...) and writes both tokens into the POSTed FormData. It resolves cleanly via the AST locator (lines 5519-5642) and passes the brace-balance check (acorn parses its password-strength regex literals correctly), so it is a valid complete-function span. The value-construction chain it drives is graded as helpers: n (sm32) 0.7, i (sm2) 0.5, c (dispatcher) 0.2, o (sm3nokey sibling) 0.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The login submit handler accountSubmit (captured as the 1.json answer): it binds the password to sm32 and the username to sm2nokey via the encrypt entry Object(h.b)(...) and writes the resulting tokens into the POSTed request. The sm32 function n (0.7), the sm2 helper i (0.5), the dispatcher c (0.2) and the sm3nokey sibling o (0) are graded below it.

behavior_category.subtype: password via SM3-then-SM2 (sm32); username via SM2 (sm2nokey)
behavior_category.recompute_check: SM2 encryption is randomized; not reproducible to a fixed value

near_categories.why_not: A single credential field (password) is tokenized; this is a per-field token derivation.
The value is keyed SM crypto of user input, not a UI-state encoding.

evidence: Minified webpack bundle (single-letter functions n/i/o/c); the sm-crypto wrapper is one module among many.
Password (sm32 -> n) and username (sm2nokey -> i) share the sm2 helper; n vs i vs c (dispatcher) are easy to confuse.
The dispatcher c selects the scheme by an EncryptType enum value; the actual algorithm is two modules deep (193c -> 8060).
